- scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh: clarify_image_build(), lines 51-53 (the prebuilt-pull success path) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After the prebuilt-image pull succeeds, the function calls `sandbox_image.sh build` and returns without running the mirror pre-seed.
  WHY: If `sandbox_image.sh build`'s own pull of the prebuilt image fails (label mismatch, network issue, image deleted between pulls), it falls back to a local docker build. That local build needs the Dockerfile's FROM image, which is not present locally (the prebuilt image is the final sandbox image, not the FROM base), so it pulls from Docker Hub and can fail with the 429 this PR is intended to prevent.
- changelog.d/7215-clarify-base-image-preseed-all-callers.md: second paragraph, "scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh runs it right before it builds the sandbox image, so every caller of that script seeds the image"
  PROBLEM: The changelog says every caller seeds the image, but the last autofix run changed `clarify_image_build` to try the prebuilt GHCR image first and run the mirror pre-seed only before a local build.
  WHY: Nothing breaks, but the release note describes behavior the code no longer has. An operator investigating an unseeded run (when the prebuilt image pulled successfully) would be misled by the changelog. The "Extra wait" table row ("at most 2 × 300 s") also omits the two prebuilt-pull attempts (up to 60 s each) that precede the pre-seed.
